sources.citation: R.I.M. Dunbar (1992). Neocortex size as a constraint on group size in primates. Journal of Human Evolution.
sources.notes: Foundational primary study (1992) in Journal of Human Evolution establishing the core experimental paradigm and quantitative parameters.

sources.citation: R.I.M. Dunbar (1995). Neocortex size and group size in primates: a test of the hypothesis. Journal of Human Evolution.
sources.notes: Empirical replication testing the primate neocortex-ratio to mean social-group-size regression across anthropoid species.

sources.citation: R. A. Hill, R. I. M. Dunbar (2003). Social network size in humans. Human Nature.
sources.notes: Empirical study of modern human Christmas-card social networks confirming a ~150 active relationship layer.

sources.citation: Patrik Lindenfors, Andreas Wartel, Johan Lind (2021). ‘Dunbar's number’ deconstructed. Biology Letters.
sources.notes: Phylogenetic Bayesian reanalysis demonstrating wide 95% confidence intervals around point estimates of Dunbar's number.

sources.citation: H. Kudo, R.I.M. Dunbar (2001). Neocortex size and social network size in primates. Animal Behaviour.
sources.notes: Comparative primate analysis demonstrating grooming clique size and coalition network scaling with neocortical volume.

sources.citation: P. S. Rodman (1989). Primate Behavior Primate Social Systems R. I. M. Dunbar. BioScience.
sources.notes: Subsequent empirical and theoretical investigation (1989) in BioScience extending the foundational findings.
